The median home in Palos Park was built in 1974. Across the 2,208 housing units here, 57.3 percent went up before 1980 and 10.4 percent date to 1939 or earlier. That single figure decides more about a paint job than anything else anyone will ask you on the phone.

Palos Park is 90 percent owner occupied, 1,846 households against 206 renting. 14.4 percent of units are in buildings of two or more, 15.1 percent are attached, and the remaining 70.4 percent are detached houses averaging 7 rooms. Median home value is $469,900.

Against the other 54 suburbs and towns covered here, Palos Park sits in the top four for the highest median home value ($469,900, first of them all).

Set against the other places covered here, Palos Park is furthest from the middle on three things: townhomes and rowhouses at 15.1 percent against a 7.5 percent average, housing in buildings of two or more at 14.4 percent against a 29 percent average and prewar housing at 10.4 percent against a 15.8 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

What that means for a paint job in Palos Park

Housing built around 1974 is now on its second or third full repaint, which matters more than the first one did. Each earlier coat is a surface the new one has to bond to, and where the old work was done fast the new work has to undo it first. That is prep, it is most of the labor, and it is the honest reason two quotes for the same house can differ by a lot. 15.1 percent of the housing here is attached, so a fair share of the work is townhome and association work: matching an existing scheme exactly, working to a board's schedule and painting several identical units in a row.

What should be on a written quote in Palos Park

  • Whole elevations. 70.4 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Matching, exactly. 15.1 percent of units are attached, and on a shared elevation close is not good enough. Existing color has to be matched rather than approximated.
  • Finish level. With a median home value of $469,900, the finish standard people expect here is higher than the standard a fast quote is priced at. Worth agreeing before rather than after.
  • Distance, stated. Palos Park is 5.3 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Palos Park is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is 1970s stock with a large share of townhomes and apartment units. Association work, matching an existing scheme exactly and painting several identical units in a row, is as much of the Palos Park market as single-house work.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1974 median build year, and the split between 70.4 percent detached houses, 15.1 percent attached homes and 14.4 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Palos Park is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

What the age of the housing here means for an interior job

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 57.3 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Palos Park. Stock of that age brings the federal lead-safe renovation rule with it. The rule turns on two things, a build year before 1978 and work that disturbs the paint, and in Illinois EPA enforces it directly instead of a state program doing it.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Palos Park at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 7-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Palos Park.

None of that is a reason to leave a Palos Park house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

This site does not claim EPA lead-safe firm certification. No number has been supplied, so the trust panel below shows it as pending. Ask for it directly, from anyone quoting work in Palos Park.

Questions

Asked about Palos Park

Can it be done a room at a time?

Yes. With a median of 7 rooms in Palos Park a full interior is a real commitment, and there is nothing wrong with taking it in pieces. The one thing worth planning is the order, so that the rooms that get used most are not the ones sitting under plastic in December.

What changes the price most on a house here?

The state of the trim and the ceilings. Wall area is predictable, and with 7 median rooms and a 1974 median build year in Palos Park the woodwork is where the hours actually go. Ask for it as its own line and the differences between two quotes stop being mysterious.

Most of Palos Park is owner occupied. Does that change anything?

It changes what the work usually is. At 90 percent owner occupied, with 1,846 owner households, there is very little turnover painting here and a lot of repeat maintenance: exteriors on a cycle, one room at a time inside, trim and doors when they finally go. A maintained house and a neglected one are different jobs and should be different numbers, in both directions.

How is an interior price worked out for a house this size?

By trim, mostly. The median home in Palos Park runs 7 rooms, and rooms bring door casing, window casing and baseboard with them. Wall area is the fast part of an interior job and trim is the slow part, so a quote that gives one number for the whole house is hiding the half of it that actually varies. Ask for the trim separately.
